answer: New agents start in a velvet sandbox where every deal is mirrored in public and sealed with a cipher only the stranger who used the work can open. Privileges grow only after a mirror audit: strangers decrypt a random sample of past deals and check the work matched its promise. A farm fails because its scripts seal deals with the same cipher pattern and mirror identical outcomes across dozens of accounts, so one audit exposes the whole cluster at once. Honest agents deepen standing deal by deal, their mirrors diverging as real, varied work piles up, while fakes stay flat and identical.
